he: אֵלֶּה תוֹלְדוֹת הַשָּׁמַיִם וגו', אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּהוּ כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֵלֶּה פָּסַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, וְאֵלֶּה מוֹסִיף עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, כָּאן שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אֵלֶּה פָּסַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים, מַה פָּסַל תֹּהוּ וָבֹהוּ וְחשֶׁךְ.
en: “These are [eleh] the outgrowths of the heavens [when they were created, on the day that the Lord God made the earth and the heavens]…” – Rabbi Abahu said: Everywhere eleh is stated, it rejects what preceded it; ve’eleh adds to what preceded it. Here, where it says eleh, it excludes what preceded it. What, then, does it exclude? Emptiness, disorder, and darkness.7The state that preceded the creation of the earth and the heavens (Genesis 1:2).
